title: The killing of Baron Wilkins by Yellow Charleston
summary: He says Italian gangsters used a deprived addict, Yellow Charleston, to shoot Baron, and Harlem sportsmen hunted him.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But then, the Italians come in, I think it was mostly the Italians. And they tricked the blacks by one

thing. They got hold of a black man that was a dope fiend. Yellow Charleston. They got ahold of Yellow Charleston and they shut him off, isolated him from all dope. Until he was like this. They told him, "Look, if you want to get dope and all the dope you want, you've got to shoot Old Man Baron." And he shot, he killed Old Man Baron. Right in front of his place. Right there at 7th Avenue and 134th Street.

After I left. At that time, I was working at the Nest. In 1923. And he killed Old Man Baron, right there. And then they didn't protect him, either. The boys around there, Bob Hewlitt and all of the boys, the sportsmen, or gangsters, or pimps, or whatever you want to call them, that was around there. They run all night, two nights, looking and trying to find, Finally said Yellow Charleston. But the white gangsters had hid him for awhile.

But nobody was able, amongst the black boys like Johnny and Mal and Bob Hewlitt, was a legendary character around there. He was a big gangster. And Bully Hall, and these fellows. DESVERNY was one of them, was one of the guys around there that he went to the war in the 15th as a Buck Private. When he came back, was a Second Lieutenant. He got decorated right on the field.
